task.amb_user_query: Create a system that automatically labels wages based on competitive rates. Add a column for this classification. Make sure it handles conversions properly when triggered.
task.follow_up_query: Thanks. Now, can you tell me the percentage of all wages that are classified as 'Premium'?
task.gt_sql_followup:
SELECT
    CAST(
        SUM(CASE WHEN wage_tier = 'Premium' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 /
        NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0)
    AS NUMERIC(5, 2)) AS premium_wage_percentage
FROM
    prevailing_wage;

entries.description: Calculates the percentage difference between offered wage and prevailing wage.
entries.definition: WDR = ((Offered Wage - Prevailing Wage) / Prevailing Wage) × 100%. Both offered and prevailing wages are converted to the same payment unit (hourly, weekly, or annually) before calculation. Wage information is included in the wage determination data.

entries.description: Classifies data flows with strong security controls.
entries.definition: A data flow where SRS = 3

entries.description: Categorizes wage offers based on their competitiveness in the labor market.
entries.definition: Wage offers are classified as Below-Market (WDR < 0%), Market-Competitive (0% ≤ WDR ≤ 10%), or Premium (WDR > 10%), indicating how employers position their compensation relative to minimum requirements. Wage information is included in the wage determination data.

entries.description: Measures how efficiently incidents are resolved relative to SLA compliance.
entries.definition: IRE = \text{SLApct} / (\text{AvgResolHrs} + 1), \text{where SLApct and AvgResolHrs are from RiskManagement, adding 1 to avoid division by zero.}

entries.description: Measures the efficiency of data transfers based on success rate and error count.
entries.definition: DTE = \frac{\text{SuccessPct}}{\text{ErrTally} + 1}

entries.description: Illustrates the different types of work visas available in the employment-based immigration system.
entries.definition: The visa classification system includes several types: H-1B (specialty occupations requiring theoretical and practical application of specialized knowledge), H-1B1 Singapore (Singapore nationals in specialty occupations), H-1B1 Chile (Chilean nationals in specialty occupations), and E-3 Australian (Australian nationals in specialty occupations).

entries.description: Quantifies how close a data flow is to saturating available bandwidth.
entries.definition: BSI = \text{BwidthPct} \times \frac{\text{DataSizeMB}}{\text{DurMin}}

entries.description: Illustrates what it means for an employer to be H-1B dependent.
entries.definition: An employer is considered H-1B dependent when the proportion of H-1B workers relative to the total workforce exceeds specific thresholds: 15% for employers with more than 50 employees, 8 workers for employers with 26-50 employees, or 4 workers for employers with 25 or fewer employees. H-1B dependent employers face additional attestation requirements. This status is tracked as part of the application data.

entries.description: Calculates the overall risk exposure by combining risk assessment and residual risk.
entries.definition: RES = \text{RiskAssess} \times \text{CtrlEff}^{-1}

entries.description: Illustrates what constitutes a willful violator designation for employers.
entries.definition: A willful violator is an employer who has been found by the Department of Labor to have committed a willful failure to meet LCA conditions or made a misrepresentation of material fact on an LCA within the past 5 years. Such employers face additional attestation requirements similar to H-1B dependent employers. This status is tracked as part of the application data.

entries.description: Evaluates the cost of compliance relative to potential penalties.
entries.definition: CCR = \frac{\text{CostUSD}}{\text{PenUSD} + 1}

entries.description: Illustrates what defines a full-time position in visa applications.
entries.definition: A full-time position typically means employment for at least 35 hours per week, though specific definitions may vary by employer. Non-full-time positions may include part-time roles that require fewer hours per week. This indicator is recorded as part of the application data.

entries.description: Quantifies the sensitivity of data based on volume and sensitivity level.
entries.definition: DSI = \text{VolGB} \times \begin{cases} 3 & \text{if DataSense = 'High'} \\ 2 & \text{if DataSense = 'Medium'} \\ 1 & \text{if DataSense = 'Low'} \end{cases}

entries.description: Illustrates the meaning of the four wage levels in the prevailing wage system.
entries.definition: Prevailing wage levels range from I to IV, representing increasingly higher wages based on skill, experience, education, and responsibility: Level I (entry-level), Level II (qualified), Level III (experienced), and Level IV (fully competent). These levels are determined based on the position's requirements compared to the occupational standard. Wage level information is included in the wage determination data.

entries.description: Measures the strength of security controls based on encryption and access controls.
entries.definition: SRS = \begin{cases} 3 & \text{if EncState = 'Full' and AclState = 'Strong'} \\ 2 & \text{if EncState = 'Full' or AclState = 'Adequate'} \\ 1 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}

entries.description: Illustrates the purpose and meaning of NAICS codes in the context of visa applications.
entries.definition: The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is a 6-digit code that identifies the employer's primary industry sector. For example, code 541511 represents 'Custom Computer Programming Services', while 561320 represents 'Temporary Help Services'. These codes help categorize employers by industry for statistical and regulatory purposes. The NAICS code is part of the employer's profile information.

entries.description: Assesses vendor reliability based on security rating and contract status.
entries.definition: VRI = \text{VendSecRate value} \times \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if ContrState = 'Active'} \\ 0.5 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}

entries.description: Illustrates the Standard Occupational Classification system used in labor certification applications.
entries.definition: The Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) code is a standardized numbering system that identifies and classifies occupations. For example, 15-1253.00 represents 'Software Quality Assurance Analysts and Testers', while 29-1141.00 represents 'Registered Nurses'. These codes help ensure that foreign workers are properly classified and paid according to their occupational category. The SOC code is included in the job information for each application.

entries.description: Quantifies the severity of audit findings based on critical findings.
entries.definition: AFS = \frac{\text{CritFindNum}}{\text{FindTally} + 1}

entries.description: Illustrates the different units of payment used in wage reporting.
entries.definition: Wage payment units indicate how wages are calculated and paid, with common units including: Hour (payment calculated per working hour), Week (payment calculated as a weekly salary), Month (payment calculated as a monthly salary), and Year (payment calculated as an annual salary). Different units may be used depending on industry norms and position types. Wage unit information is included in the wage determination data.

entries.description: Measures the workload from data subject requests.
entries.definition: DSRL = \text{AccReqNum} + \text{DelReqNum} + \text{RectReqNum} + \text{PortReqNum}

entries.description: Illustrates the significance of attorney representation in visa applications.
entries.definition: Attorney representation status indicates whether an employer has legal counsel for the visa application process. When present, it shows the employer has retained qualified legal assistance for navigating immigration regulations. When absent, it indicates the employer is self-represented, handling the application process internally without specialized legal counsel. This status is tracked as part of the application process.

entries.description: Evaluates risk associated with cross-border data transfers.
entries.definition: CBRF = \text{RES} \times \begin{cases} 2 & \text{if OrigNation \neq DestNation} \\ 1 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}

entries.description: Illustrates the choices employers have regarding public disclosure of their business information.
entries.definition: Employers can choose whether their business information is publicly disclosed in the visa application process. 'Disclose Business' indicates the employer consents to having their information publicly available, while other options may restrict disclosure to protect confidential business information. Disclosure choices are recorded as part of the application data.

entries.description: Identifies data flows with elevated risk based on risk exposure and sensitivity.
entries.definition: A data flow where RES > 0.7 and DSI > 100

entries.description: Calculates the number of days between application receipt and decision.
entries.definition: APT is the number of days between the date the application is received and the date a decision is made. Both dates are recorded as part of the application data.

entries.description: Identifies vendors failing compliance standards.
entries.definition: A vendor where PolComp = 'Non-compliant' or ProcComp = 'Non-compliant'

entries.description: Calculates the percentage of certified applications out of total applications.
entries.definition: AR = (Number of Certified Applications / Total Number of Applications) × 100%. Application status is tracked as part of the application data.

entries.description: Flags audits with significant issues requiring urgent remediation.
entries.definition: An audit where AFS > 0.5

entries.description: Measures the number of cases handled by each attorney.
entries.definition: ACL is the total number of cases handled by each attorney. Attorney assignment is tracked as part of the application process.

entries.description: Highlights data profiles with high sensitivity and weak security.
entries.definition: A data profile where DSI > 100 and SRS < 2

entries.description: Measures the proportion of H-1B applications submitted by an employer relative to all applications.
entries.definition: EHC = (Number of H-1B Applications by Employer / Total Number of H-1B Applications) × 100%. Visa classification and employer information are tracked in the application data.

entries.description: Identifies compliance issues in cross-border data flows.
entries.definition: A compliance record where GdprComp = 'Non-compliant' or LocLawComp = 'Non-compliant' and OrigNation ≠ DestNation

entries.description: Measures the number of visa workers per worksite.
entries.definition: WD = (Number of Workers at Worksite / Number of Worksites). Worksite and worker information are recorded as part of the application data.

entries.description: Categorizes vendors into risk tiers based on security and compliance.
entries.definition: A vendor is: High Risk if VRI < 2, Medium Risk if 2 ≤ VRI < 3, Low Risk if VRI ≥ 3

entries.description: Measures how much more an employer pays compared to minimum requirements.
entries.definition: WPR = ((Offered Wage - Minimum Required Wage) / Minimum Required Wage) × 100%. Minimum required wage is typically the prevailing wage or higher depending on regulations. Wage information is included in the wage determination data.

entries.description: Identifies data profiles with failed integrity checks.
entries.definition: A data profile where IntCheck = 'Failed' or CsumVerify = 'Failed'

entries.description: Measures the success rate of applications by employer.
entries.definition: ASR = (Number of Certified Applications by Employer / Total Applications by Employer) × 100%. Employer and application status are tracked as part of the application data.

entries.description: Flags data flows with high bandwidth saturation and low efficiency.
entries.definition: A data flow where BSI > 50 and DTE < 1.0

entries.description: Measures the percentage of applications in each state.
entries.definition: SAD = (Number of Applications in State / Total Number of Applications) × 100%. State information is included in the worksite data.

entries.description: Identifies data flows with high regulatory risk due to compliance gaps and cross-border transfers.
entries.definition: A data flow with CBRF > 1.5 and Cross-Border Compliance Gap exists

entries.description: Measures the percentage of applications in each industry based on NAICS codes.
entries.definition: IAD = (Number of Applications in Industry / Total Number of Applications) × 100%. Industry is determined by the employer's NAICS code.

entries.description: Illustrates the success rate of data transfers.
entries.definition: Ranges from 0 to 100%. A SuccessPct of 95% indicates reliable transfers, while <80% suggests frequent failures, from DataFlow.

entries.description: Measures the relative demand for specific occupations based on SOC codes.
entries.definition: ODI = (Number of Applications for SOC Code / Average Applications per SOC Code). SOC code information is included in the job data for each application.

entries.description: Illustrates the risk assessment score.
entries.definition: Ranges from 0 to 100. A RiskAssess > 80 indicates high risk, while <20 suggests minimal risk, from RiskManagement.

entries.description: Adjusts offered wage based on city's cost of living index.
entries.definition: CLAW = (Offered Wage / Cost of Living Index) × 100, where the Cost of Living Index is a standardized index with 100 as the national average. Wage and location information are included in the application data.

entries.description: Illustrates the volume of data in gigabytes.
entries.definition: Ranges from 0 to millions. A VolGB of 1000 might represent a large dataset, while 0.1 is typical for small logs, from DataProfile.

entries.description: Measures the concentration of applications in different months of the year.
entries.definition: SAI = (Number of Applications in Month / Average Monthly Applications). Application receipt dates are tracked as part of the application data.

entries.description: Illustrates the encryption status of data.
entries.definition: Enum: 'Full', 'Partial'. 'Full' indicates all data is encrypted, while 'Partial' suggests gaps, from SecurityProfile.

entries.description: Measures the certification rate of applications handled by each attorney.
entries.definition: ASR = (Number of Certified Applications by Attorney / Total Applications by Attorney) × 100%. Attorney assignment and application status are tracked as part of the application process.

entries.description: Illustrates the vendor security rating.
entries.definition: Enum: 'A' = 4, 'B' = 3, 'C' = 2, 'D' or others = 1. This numeric scale quantifies vendor security, where 'A' reflects top-tier security (score 4), and lower ratings (down to 'D') indicate progressively weaker security controls.

entries.description: Measures the percentage of continuation applications by an employer.
entries.definition: ERR = (Number of Continuation Applications / Total Number of Applications by Employer) × 100%. Employer and application type are tracked as part of the application data.

entries.description: Illustrates GDPR compliance status.
entries.definition: Enum: 'Compliant', 'Non-compliant', 'Partial'. 'Compliant' meets all GDPR rules, 'Non-compliant' fails key requirements, from Compliance.

entries.description: Measures the percentage of applications using external legal counsel.
entries.definition: ECR = (Number of Applications with Attorney / Total Number of Applications) × 100%. Attorney assignment is tracked as part of the application process.

entries.description: Illustrates the response time for data subject requests.
entries.definition: Ranges from 0 to days. A RespTimeDay of 1.5 suggests quick responses, while >7 indicates delays, from AuditAndCompliance.

entries.description: Measures the diversity of an employer's worksites across different geographic areas.
entries.definition: WDI = 1 - sum((Number of Workers at Worksite i / Total Workers)^2) for all worksites. Worksite and worker information are included in the application data.

entries.description: Illustrates the count of errors in data transfers.
entries.definition: Integer ≥ 0. An ErrTally of 0 indicates flawless transfers, while >10 suggests reliability issues, from DataFlow.

entries.description: Measures how competitive an employer's offered wage is compared to industry average.
entries.definition: WCI = (Employer Average Offered Wage / Industry Average Offered Wage). Wage and industry information are included in the application data.

entries.description: Illustrates the effectiveness of risk controls.
entries.definition: Ranges from 0 to 100. A CtrlEff of 90% shows strong controls, while <50% indicates weaknesses, from RiskManagement.

entries.description: Measures the percentage distribution of different visa classifications.
entries.definition: VCD = (Number of Applications for Visa Class / Total Number of Applications) × 100%. Visa classification is tracked as part of the application data.

entries.description: Illustrates the retention period for audit logs.
entries.definition: Integer ≥ 0 days. A LogRetDays of 365 meets many compliance needs, while <30 may violate regulations, from SecurityProfile.

entries.description: Quantifies the relative size of an employer based on number of visa applications.
entries.definition: ESI = (Employer Number of Applications / Average Applications per Employer). Employer and application information are tracked as part of the application data.

entries.description: Quantifies the reliability of a data flow based on success rate and retry attempts.
entries.definition: DFRS = \text{DTE} \times (1 - \text{RtryTally} / (\text{ErrTally} + 1))

entries.description: Measures the average wage differential in each industry.
entries.definition: IWD = (Sum of Wage Differential Rates in Industry / Number of Applications in Industry). Wage and industry information are included in the application data.

entries.description: Evaluates the cost-effectiveness of security controls relative to compliance costs.
entries.definition: SCCR = \text{SRS} / (\text{CostUSD} + 1)

entries.description: Measures the efficiency of application processing relative to average times.
entries.definition: PER = (Average Processing Time / Application Processing Time), where values above 1 indicate faster than average processing. Processing time is calculated from application receipt and decision dates.

entries.description: Measures the compliance burden of a vendor based on audit findings and security rating.
entries.definition: VCB = \text{AFS} \times (5 - \text{VendSecRate value})

entries.description: Measures the geographic concentration of visa applications.
entries.definition: GCI = sum((Applications in State i / Total Applications)^2) for all states. State and application information are included in the application data.

entries.description: Assesses risk from large cross-border data volumes.
entries.definition: CDVR = \text{CBRF} \times \text{VolGB}

entries.description: Measures how specialized an attorney is in specific visa types.
entries.definition: ASI = 1 - (Number of Different Visa Types Handled by Attorney / Total Number of Visa Types), where values closer to 1 indicate higher specialization. Attorney and visa type information are tracked as part of the application process.

entries.description: Quantifies pressure from data subject requests relative to response time.
entries.definition: DSRP = \text{DSRL} \times \text{RespTimeDay}

entries.description: Measures the concentration of applications across industries.
entries.definition: ICR = sum((Applications in Industry i / Total Applications)^2) for all industries. Industry and application information are included in the application data.

entries.description: Measures the extent of encryption coverage relative to data sensitivity.
entries.definition: ECR = \text{SRS} \times \text{DSI}

entries.description: Measures the annual percentage increase in offered wages for similar positions.
entries.definition: WGR = ((Current Year Average Wage - Previous Year Average Wage) / Previous Year Average Wage) × 100%. Wage and year information are included in the application data.

entries.description: Calculates the workload required for audit remediation based on findings and compliance gaps.
entries.definition: ARL = \text{AFS} \times \text{DSRL}

entries.description: Quantifies the complexity of a visa application based on multiple factors.
entries.definition: ACS is calculated as a weighted sum of factors such as H-1B dependency, willful violator status, new employment, and amendment status. Each factor is represented as a binary indicator in the application data.

entries.description: Evaluates risk from bandwidth overuse in sensitive data flows.
entries.definition: BRF = \text{BSI} \times \text{DSI}

entries.description: Compares the cost of living at a worksite relative to the national average.
entries.definition: WkCI = (Worksite Cost of Living / National Average Cost of Living) × 100. Worksite and cost of living information are included in the application data.

entries.description: Quantifies how vendor issues amplify overall risk exposure.
entries.definition: VRA = \text{VRI} \times \text{RES}

entries.description: Measures the percentage of applications using premium processing.
entries.definition: PPR = (Number of Premium Processing Applications / Total Number of Applications) × 100%. Premium processing status is tracked as part of the application data.

entries.description: Identifies data flows with both high risk exposure and poor reliability.
entries.definition: A data flow where RES > 0.7 and DFRS < 0.5

entries.description: Defines positions that offer significantly higher wages than required.
entries.definition: A position is considered a premium wage position if the Wage Differential Rate (WDR) exceeds 20%, indicating the employer is offering significantly above the prevailing wage. Wage information is included in the wage determination data.

entries.description: Flags data flows with high compliance costs and audit remediation needs.
entries.definition: A data flow where CCR > 0.8 and ARL > 10

entries.description: Categorizes the timing of visa application submissions relative to employment start date.
entries.definition: The visa filing window represents when applications are submitted relative to the intended employment start date. Applications are categorized as: 'Optimal Window (4-6 Months)' before start date, 'Early Filing' (more than 6 months before), '1-3 Months Before', 'Same Month', or 'After Start Date'. These categories help analyze filing patterns and potential processing challenges. Submission and start dates are tracked as part of the application data.

entries.description: Identifies sensitive data lacking adequate encryption coverage.
entries.definition: A data profile where DSI > 100 and ECR < 2

entries.description: Defines industries that heavily rely on foreign workers through visa programs.
entries.definition: An industry is considered visa-dependent if the percentage of visa applications relative to the total workforce exceeds 15%, indicating significant reliance on foreign talent. Industry information is determined by the employer's NAICS code.

entries.description: Highlights data flows under strain from data subject requests and bandwidth saturation.
entries.definition: A data flow where DSRP > 50 and BSI > 50

entries.description: Identifies occupations with demonstrated shortages of qualified U.S. workers.
entries.definition: Occupations with significant shortages of qualified U.S. workers are identified by a Wage Differential Rate (WDR) exceeding 10% and a statistically significant number of applications. These occupations may receive prioritized processing or cap exemptions.

entries.description: Identifies data flows with elevated risk due to vendor issues.
entries.definition: A data flow where VRA > 3 and VCB > 2

entries.description: Identifies geographic areas with concentrated visa application activity.
entries.definition: A geographic area (such as a state, metropolitan area, or city) is considered a hotspot if the volume of visa applications is at least 50% higher than the national average when adjusted for population. Location information is included in the worksite data.

entries.description: Flags cross-border data flows with significant audit issues.
entries.definition: A data flow where CDVR > 1000 and AFS > 0.5

entries.description: Categorizes attorneys based on their visa application specialization patterns.
entries.definition: Attorneys are classified as Specialists (over 80% of cases in one visa type), Generalists (even distribution across visa types), or Hybrid Practitioners (significant experience in 2-3 visa categories). Attorney and visa type information are tracked as part of the application process.

entries.description: Identifies high-volume data flows with weak security controls.
entries.definition: A data flow where VolGB > 500 and SRS < 2

entries.description: Categorizes employers based on their scale of visa usage.
entries.definition: Employers are classified as Small-scale users (fewer than 5 applications annually), Medium-scale users (5-25 applications annually), or Large-scale users (more than 25 applications annually). Employer and application information are tracked as part of the application data.

entries.description: Highlights data flows with both regulatory risk and compliance gaps.
entries.definition: A data flow with Regulatory Risk Exposure and GdprComp = 'Non-compliant'

entries.description: Defines the possible status outcomes for visa applications.
entries.definition: Possible outcomes for a visa application include: Certified (approved), Denied (rejected), Withdrawn (voluntarily withdrawn by applicant), and Certified-Withdrawn (approved but later withdrawn). Application status is tracked as part of the application data.

entries.description: Identifies data flows where bandwidth saturation amplifies risk.
entries.definition: A data flow where BRF > 100 and RES > 0.7

entries.description: Categorizes positions based on their level of specialization.
entries.definition: Job positions are classified as General (broad knowledge required), Specialized (focused expertise in one area), or Highly Specialized (deep expertise in niche areas), typically correlated with wage level and experience requirements. Job and wage information are included in the application data.

entries.description: Flags data flows with poor incident resolution and high risk.
entries.definition: A data flow where IRE < 0.5 and High-Risk Data Flow

entries.description: Defines patterns in visa application timing throughout the year.
entries.definition: Seasonal patterns in visa application submissions include Peak Season (periods with higher submission rates), Off-Peak Season (lower submission rates), and Transition Periods (moderate activity between peaks). Application receipt dates are tracked as part of the application data.

entries.description: Quantifies the stability of data flows by balancing reliability and error recovery.
entries.definition: DFSI = \text{DFRS} \times \frac{\text{SuccessPct}}{\text{ErrTally} + 1}

entries.description: Categorizes applications based on their procedural complexity.
entries.definition: Applications are classified as Standard (straightforward cases), or Complex (cases involving H-1B dependency, willful violator status, or special attestations). Complexity factors are tracked as part of the application data.

entries.description: Measures the operational burden of compliance relative to data subject request load.
entries.definition: COR = \text{DSRP} / (\text{CostUSD} + 1)

entries.description: Categorizes attorneys based on their application success rates.
entries.definition: Attorneys are rated as High Performers (over 95% approval rate), Standard Performers (85-95% approval rate), or Underperformers (below 85% approval rate), based on their application outcomes.

entries.description: Evaluates the maturity of security controls based on encryption and audit log retention.
entries.definition: SPM = \text{ECR} \times \frac{\text{LogRetDays}}{365}

entries.description: Categorizes employers based on the geographic spread of their worksites.
entries.definition: Employers are classified as Single-Location (all applications for one location), Regional (multiple locations in one region), or National (multiple regions), reflecting operational breadth. Worksite information is included in the application data.

entries.description: Assesses the concentration of risk from a vendor’s compliance and security issues.
entries.definition: VRC = \text{VRA} \times (1 - \text{VRI})

entries.description: Categorizes the degree to which employers rely on visa programs.
entries.definition: Employers are classified as Low Dependency (less than 5% of workforce), Moderate Dependency (5-15%), or High Dependency (over 15%). H-1B dependent status typically applies to the high dependency category.

entries.description: Quantifies compliance risk for cross-border flows based on regulatory gaps and volume.
entries.definition: CBCE = \text{CDVR} \times \begin{cases} 2 & \text{if GdprComp = 'Non-compliant'} \\ 1 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}

entries.description: Categorizes positions based on the scarcity of qualified candidates.
entries.definition: Positions are classified as Abundant (many qualified candidates), Moderate Scarcity (limited candidates), or High Scarcity (very few candidates), often correlated with wage premiums and processing priorities.

entries.description: Measures the potential impact of incidents based on risk exposure and resolution efficiency.
entries.definition: IIF = \text{RES} \times (1 - \text{IRE})

entries.description: Defines employers that consistently offer above-market wages.
entries.definition: An employer is considered a premium wage employer if their average Wage Differential Rate (WDR) across all applications exceeds 15%, indicating a consistent strategy of offering premium compensation.

entries.description: Evaluates risk from prolonged data retention relative to sensitivity.
entries.definition: DRRS = \text{DSI} \times \frac{\text{RetDays}}{365}

entries.description: Categorizes applications based on their risk of processing delays.
entries.definition: Applications are classified as Low Risk (no special factors), Moderate Risk (1-2 complexity factors), or High Risk (3 or more complexity factors or from willful violators), based on the Application Complexity Score (ACS).

entries.description: Quantifies pressure from audit findings and compliance remediation needs.
entries.definition: ACP = \text{ARL} \times \text{AFS}

entries.description: Defines employers with regular, ongoing visa application activity.
entries.definition: An employer is considered a continuous filer if they submit visa applications in at least 9 months of the year, indicating consistent reliance on foreign worker programs.

entries.description: Assesses compliance risk from bandwidth-constrained data flows.
entries.definition: BCR = \text{BRF} \times \begin{cases} 1.5 & \text{if GdprComp = 'Partial'} \\ 2 & \text{if GdprComp = 'Non-compliant'} \\ 1 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}

entries.description: Evaluates the effectiveness of legal representation in visa applications.
entries.definition: Legal representation efficacy is measured by comparing the approval rate of applications with attorney representation to those without. High Impact is defined as over 10% higher approval rate, Moderate Impact as 5-10% higher, and Minimal Impact as less than 5% difference.

entries.description: Evaluates the cost-effectiveness of vendor security relative to compliance burden.
entries.definition: VSCI = \text{VCB} / (\text{SCCR} + 1)

entries.description: Enumerates the acceptable alternative sources for prevailing wage determinations.
entries.definition: Acceptable sources for prevailing wage determinations include Occupational Employment Statistics (OES), Collective Bargaining Agreements (CBA), and independent published wage surveys that meet Department of Labor requirements. Source information is included in the wage determination data.

entries.description: Identifies high-risk data flows with poor stability.
entries.definition: A data flow where DFSI < 0.5 and Critical Data Flow Risk exists

entries.description: Flags data flows with high security burden and compliance exposure.
entries.definition: A data flow where SPM < 1 and CBCE > 100

entries.description: Highlights data profiles with prolonged retention and high sensitivity.
entries.definition: A data profile where DRRS > 50 and DSI > 100

entries.description: Identifies vendors contributing to concentrated compliance risks.
entries.definition: A vendor where VRC > 2 and VCB > 2

entries.description: Flags data flows with high incident impact and compliance gaps.
entries.definition: A data flow where IIF > 0.8 and GdprComp = 'Non-compliant'

entries.description: Identifies data flows under pressure from audit findings and compliance burdens.
entries.definition: A data flow where ACP > 5 and COR > 0.5.

entries.description: Highlights data flows where bandwidth constraints exacerbate compliance risks.
entries.definition: A data flow where BCR > 50 and Cross-Border Compliance Gap exists

entries.description: Identifies data flows with high vendor-related costs and risks.
entries.definition: A data flow where VSCI > 1 and VRA > 3

entries.description: Flags sensitive data flows with stability issues.
entries.definition: A data flow where DFSI < 0.5 and Sensitive Data Exposure exists

entries.description: Identifies data flows with severe audit findings and regulatory risks.
entries.definition: A data flow where Regulatory Risk Exposure exists and ACP > 5

entries.description: Describes the data flow path from origin to destination nation.
entries.definition: A string concatenating OrigNation and DestNation as 'OrigNation -> DestNation'

entries.description: Describes the types and counts of data subject requests.
entries.definition: An array of strings listing request types and their counts: 'Access: AccReqNum', 'Deletion: DelReqNum', 'Rectification: RectReqNum', 'Portability: PortReqNum', unnested for display

entries.description: Counts the number of failed integrity checks per data profile.
entries.definition: IFC = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if IntCheck = 'Failed'} \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} + \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if CsumVerify = 'Failed'} \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}

entries.description: Concatenates the types of integrity failures for a data profile into a single string.
entries.definition: A comma-separated string listing failure types: 'Integrity Check' if IntCheck = 'Failed', 'Checksum Verification' if CsumVerify = 'Failed'.

entries.description: Identifies data flows with elevated audit compliance pressure based on audit findings and data subject request load.
entries.definition: A data flow where ACP > 5

entries.description: Identifies data flows where the origin and destination nations differ.
entries.definition: A data flow where OrigNation != DestNation

entries.description: Identifies data flows where the remediation deadline has passed.

analysis.analysis_zh:
## 1. 题目要什么
建一套自动给工资打竞争力标签的机制：给 prevailing_wage 加列 wage_tier，并用触发器在插入/更新时自动算（含单位换算）。二阶段：统计所有工资中标为 'Premium' 的占比。

## 2. 关键歧义点
"automatically labels""when triggered""handles conversions"→需触发器 + 单位折年 + KB48 分档。展示版抽象，但要素明确。无需澄清。

## 3. 用到的领域知识 (KB)
- KB 11 WDR：折年后 $\frac{\text{Offered}-\text{Prevailing}}{\text{Prevailing}}\times100\%$。
- KB 48 Wage Competitiveness Tiers：Below-Market(WDR<0)、Market-Competitive(0-10)、Premium(>10)。

## 4. 写出正确 SQL 的步骤
1. `ALTER TABLE prevailing_wage ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS wage_tier TEXT`。
2. `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION update_wage_competitiveness() RETURNS TRIGGER`：从 `NEW.wage_details` 用 `REGEXP_REPLACE([^0-9\.]+)` 清洗 offered.from 与 prevailing.value，单位 `::enum_...`；按 Hour×2080/Week×52/Month×12/Year×1 折年；`wdr=((offered_annual-prevailing_annual)/prevailing_annual)*100`，prevailing 为 NULL/0 时 wdr=NULL。
3. `NEW.wage_tier=CASE WHEN wdr IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN wdr<0 'Below-Market' WHEN 0-10 'Market-Competitive' ELSE 'Premium' END; RETURN NEW;`（KB48）。
4. `DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS ...; CREATE TRIGGER wage_competitiveness_trigger BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON prevailing_wage FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION update_wage_competitiveness();`——BEFORE 行级才能改 NEW。
- 最易写错：用 AFTER 触发器（改 NEW 无效）；换算系数错；正则没加 'g' 漏清洗。

二阶段：`SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN wage_tier='Premium' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)*100.0/NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS NUMERIC(5,2)) AS premium_wage_percentage FROM prevailing_wage`。

## 5. 输出列
一阶段：prevailing_wage.wage_tier（触发器维护）。
二阶段：premium_wage_percentage。
